Mateo — attaching Nova Health's redline to the Order Form focused on Exhibit B (pricing schedule). Primary ask: carve a corridor around the committed minimum for the first 12 months (we proposed a 10% floor) and a soft cap language tied to monthly smoothing. - Cap: temporary monthly cap + true-up at quarter-end; Nova wants the cap to be 150% of baseline with a right to request credits if actual usage below floor
- Smoothing: allow revenue smoothing over a rolling 3-month window rather than immediate monthly true-ups

Matt/Team — drafting suggested redline language and a short memo on operational exposure. Key points for negotiation: 

1) Floor phase-in: accept a phased floor but tie the minimum to committed units in the order form (avoid arbitrary percentages). Suggested language: "For months 1–3, the Monthly Minimum shall be 80% of the committed monthly units; for months 4–12 the Monthly Minimum shall be 90% of the committed monthly units."

2) Cap and credits: accept a temporary Cap for burst protection only. Cap wording: "Temporary Monthly Cap = 160% of the committed monthly units. Any overage charges in a Calendaring Period above the Cap shall be subject to Provider invoicing; Provider may, at its discretion, apply a credit in the subsequent quarter if aggregate usage falls below the aggregated Monthly Minimum over the quarter." This preserves discretion and avoids an unlimited credit obligation.

3) True-up timing: counter to their 30-day ask — propose 60 days post-quarter for reconciliation to allow for internal traceability and billing cycles. Add audit rights limited to once per year and scope-limited to billing records related to the Order Form.

4) Grace for early termination triggers: include explicit carveout that credits/true-ups do not apply if Customer terminates for convenience.

I'll prepare a redlined Exhibit B and a short cover note to send to Nova. Also propose attaching the financial impact summary from Aditya.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_corridor_amendment.docx (Word, 22KB)]

Team — ran the scenarios off the pricing_schedule_v4.xlsx. Short summary (12-month view, revenue impact vs committed baseline):
- Accepting a flat 90% floor with immediate effect => downside revenue risk ~ -9% ARR in year one (concentrated in months 1–3).
- Phased floor (80% months 1–3, 90% months 4–12) reduces downside to ~ -5% ARR and smooths cashflow timing.
- Cap at 160% with discretionary credits exposure is manageable; worst-case customer-requested credits (if we voluntarily apply them) would be <= 3% ARR in stress scenario.

Recommendation: accept Laura's phased floor, set cap at 160% with discretionary credit language, and agree to a 60-day post-quarter reconciliation. This balances the customer's ask for smoothing with our revenue predictability.

I'll attach the XLS showing scenario tables.

—Aditya
Director, Revenue Operations
[Attachment: pricing_schedule_v4.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)]

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Cc: legal@novahealth.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form – Pricing corridor anchoring / Exhibit B redlines

Jared — thanks for the redline and for laying out Nova's concerns. We discussed internally and want to propose the following compromise (attached as a marked Exhibit B):

1) Floor phase-in: For months 1–3, the Monthly Minimum will be 80% of the committed monthly units; for months 4–12, the Monthly Minimum will be 90% of the committed monthly units. This gives Nova a runway while protecting Redwood's revenue ramp.

2) Cap: A Temporary Monthly Cap equal to 160% of the committed monthly units will apply for the first 12 months. Provider may invoice usage above the Cap; Provider may, in its sole discretion, apply a credit in the subsequent quarter if aggregate usage for the quarter is below the aggregated Monthly Minimum. This preserves our billing mechanics while giving Nova practical smoothing.

3) True-up timing and audit: Reconciliations will occur within 60 days after the end of each fiscal quarter. Customer audit rights are limited to once per 12-month period and restricted to billing records related to the Order Form.

4) Termination: Credits or adjustments do not apply if Customer terminates the Order Form for convenience.

Attached: redlined Exhibit B (Proposed_Corridor_Amendment.docx) and our financial scenarios. If this is acceptable, we can incorporate the language into the DocuSign package and finalize the Order Form.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up quickly.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_corridor_amendment.docx (Word, 24KB)]
